why-autonomous-mission.title: The Canyon Expedition Launches
why-autonomous-mission.content:
### The Grand Horizon of Valles Marineris

The Martian dawn breaks in shades of copper, amber, and gold across the towering cliffs of Valles Marineris. On the observation terrace, robot mascot **IRIS [ o o ]** monitors the telemetry console as the propulsion drives roar to life.

All three drones of the autonomous fleet take flight in tight formation:
- **Scout Drone Sigma** leads the vanguard, scanning deep ravines.
- **Survey Drone Delta** maps mineral deposits across the canyon floor.
- **Heavy Drone Omega** secures cargo delivery to the forward scientific base.

This final chapter is the culmination of your entire journey through C++. Every loop, every condition, every vector, function reference, struct, and defensive stream check you built has led to this moment.

Together, we will run the final autonomous navigation simulation, verify obstacle detection, track energy depletion across flight waypoints, and generate the definitive mission completion report!

mission-pipeline-architecture.title: Full Flight Simulation Architecture
mission-pipeline-architecture.content:
### The Complete Aerospace Software Pipeline

The Capstone Phase II architecture coordinates the entire mission from pre-flight checks to final touchdown:

![Autonomous Mission Pipeline](assets/l32-final2-launch.en.svg)

#### 1. Pre-Flight Fleet Qualification
- Dynamic roster: `vector<DroneReport> fleet`.
- Validates energy reserves before clearing flight paths.

#### 2. The Autonomous Simulation Engine
- Iterates through coordinate waypoints `(x, y)`.
- Evaluates Manhattan navigation cost: `abs(dx) + abs(dy)`.
- Tests proximity to geological hazards via `is_hazard()`.
- Halts execution safely if power reserves become depleted.

#### 3. Formatted Mission Debrief
- Industrial-grade formatted telemetry reports powered by `<iomanip>` (`setw`, `left`, `right`).
- Aggregates squadron flight distance, operational readiness, and final mission status.

What is printed to standard output?

Analyze this drone state update as it advances its coordinates and expends battery power.
What is printed to standard output?
inspect-flight-state-evolution.explain: `d` starts at `{0, 0, 100}`. `d.x += 15` sets x to 15, `d.y += 20` sets y to 20, and `d.battery -= 35` decreases battery to 65. The program outputs `POS:(15,20) BAT:65`.

audit-mission-loop-condition.title: Code Audit: Out-of-Bounds Iteration Bug
audit-mission-loop-condition.content:
### Spot the Off-by-One Danger

A navigational flight loop crashes when traversing its waypoint vector because the loop condition attempts to access one element beyond the vector size!

Click the loop line where `<=` is incorrectly used instead of `<`.
body: **Spot the Off-by-One Danger**
A navigational flight loop crashes when traversing its waypoint vector because the loop condition attempts to access one element beyond the vector size!
Click the loop line where `<=` is incorrectly used instead of `<`.
audit-mission-loop-condition.explain: Line 9 uses `i <= path.size()`. In 0-based indexing, valid elements range from `0` to `path.size() - 1`. The `<=` condition causes the loop to read `path[path.size()]` on the final iteration, triggering an out-of-bounds memory access. The condition must be `i < path.size()`.

write-hazard-obstacle-detector.title: Flight Navigation: Hazard Proximity Sensor
write-hazard-obstacle-detector.content:
### Collision Avoidance Gate

Implement the hazard avoidance function `is_hazard`.

A waypoint at `(x, y)` is considered a hazard if its Manhattan distance to the hazard zone `(hx, hy)` is strictly less than `safe_dist`:
`(abs(x - hx) + abs(y - hy)) < safe_dist`

Input format:
Five integers on one line: `x y hx hy safe_dist`.

Output format:
`HAZARD: 1` if within dangerous proximity, or `HAZARD: 0` if clear.
write-hazard-obstacle-detector.task:
1. Define function `bool is_hazard(int x, int y, int hx, int hy, int safe_dist)` returning `true` if `(abs(x - hx) + abs(y - hy)) < safe_dist`, and `false` otherwise.
2. In `main()`, read `x`, `y`, `hx`, `hy`, and `safe_dist` from `cin`.
3. Call `is_hazard` and output `HAZARD: <1 or 0>` followed by a newline.

predict-fleet-mission-summary.title: Diagnostics: Energy Depletion Tracing
predict-fleet-mission-summary.content:
### Predict the Output

Trace the execution of this mission power drain loop as it executes 3 successive propulsion burns.

What is the surviving battery value printed to standard output?
body: **Predict the Output**
Trace the execution of this mission power drain loop as it executes 3 successive propulsion burns.
What is the surviving battery value printed to standard output?
predict-fleet-mission-summary.explain: The loop iterates 3 times, subtracting 25 from battery on each step: `100 - (3 * 25) = 100 - 75 = 25`. The program outputs `SURVIVING BATTERY: 25`.

parsons-mission-simulation-loop.title: Modular Assembly: Safe Flight Loop
parsons-mission-simulation-loop.content:
### Assemble the Navigational Safeguard

Reorder the code blocks to construct an autonomous flight loop that steps through waypoints, deducts battery power, and safely aborts if battery reaches zero or below.
body: **Assemble the Navigational Safeguard**
Reorder the code blocks to construct an autonomous flight loop that steps through waypoints, deducts battery power, and safely aborts if battery reaches zero or below.
parsons-mission-simulation-loop.explain: Include `<iostream>` and declare `using namespace std;`. In `main()`, initialize battery to 80. Loop through waypoints, subtracting 20 each step. If battery drops to or below 0, output `ABORT` and exit. After completing the loop, output `SURVIVED: <battery>`.

write-drone-flight-simulator.title: Avionics Core: Multi-Waypoint Flight Simulator
write-drone-flight-simulator.content:
### Trajectory Simulation Engine

Simulate an autonomous drone expedition from origin `(0, 0)` across `n` waypoints.

Input:
1. Two integers: `battery` and `n` (number of waypoints).
2. `n` pairs of coordinates: `x y`.

Simulation Rules:
- Current position begins at `(0, 0)`.
- Moving to `(x, y)` costs `cost = abs(x - cur_x) + abs(y - cur_y)` battery units.
- If `cost > battery`, the drone cannot reach the waypoint: immediately print `MISSION ABORTED` and terminate the simulation.
- Otherwise, deduct `cost` from `battery` and update current position to `(x, y)`.
- If all `n` waypoints are reached without failure, print:
  `MISSION SUCCESS`
  `REMAINING BATTERY: <battery>`
  `FINAL POS: (<cur_x>, <cur_y>)`
write-drone-flight-simulator.task:
1. In `main()`, read `battery` and `n` from `cin`.
2. Initialize `cur_x = 0`, `cur_y = 0`, and `bool aborted = false`.
3. Loop `n` times reading `x` and `y`.
4. If `abs(x - cur_x) + abs(y - cur_y) > battery`, output `MISSION ABORTED`, set `aborted = true`, and break.
5. Otherwise deduct movement cost from `battery` and update coordinates.
6. If not aborted, output `MISSION SUCCESS`, `REMAINING BATTERY: <battery>`, and `FINAL POS: (<cur_x>, <cur_y>)`.

capstone-stage2-grand-finale.title: Capstone Phase II: Grand Squadron Mission Director
capstone-stage2-grand-finale.content:
### The Grand Mission Debrief

Construct the final mission control debriefing program that compiles squadron telemetry into an executive flight board.

Input format:
1. Integer `n` (number of drones in squadron).
2. `n` lines, each containing:
   `int id`, `string name`, `int battery`, `int distance`, `string status`.

Processing & Output:
1. Output formatted table header:
   `DRONE        BATTERY    DISTANCE      STATUS`
   (Columns: name left-aligned width 8, battery right width 10, distance right width 12, status right width 12).
2. For each drone, output its record with identical alignments and widths.
3. Output `TOTAL DISTANCE: <sum of distance> KM`.
4. Output `FLEET STATUS: <n> DRONES OPERATIONAL`.
capstone-stage2-grand-finale.task:
1. Read integer `n` and store drone reports into `vector<DroneReport> fleet`.
2. Output the table header using `left << setw(8) << "DRONE" << right << setw(10) << "BATTERY" << setw(12) << "DISTANCE" << setw(12) << "STATUS"`.
3. Loop over `fleet` and print each drone row with identical column widths.
4. Calculate total distance and output `TOTAL DISTANCE: <total_dist> KM`.
5. Output `FLEET STATUS: <n> DRONES OPERATIONAL`.

recap.title: Mission Accomplished: Course Graduation!
recap.content:
### Congratulations, Flight Engineer!

You have successfully completed all 32 chapters of **C++ Programming: Mission IRIS**!

#### Your Journey from Rookie to Aerospace Software Engineer

```
[Chapter 1: First Pulse]  ──>  Hello World, Output Streams, Compilers
          │
[Chapters 2–8: Flight Systems] ──>  Types, Math, Logic, Branching, Loops
          │
[Chapters 9–16: Navigation] ──>  Array Memories, Traversal, 2D Radar, Algorithms
          │
[Chapters 17–24: Fleet Core] ──>  Vectors, Dynamic Storage, Functions, Scope, References
          │
[Chapters 25–30: Avionics Bus] ──>  Strings, iomanip Formatting, Structs, fstream Files, Defensive IO
          │
[Chapters 31–32: Capstone] ──>  Full Autonomous Multi-Drone Space Mission Architecture!
```

#### What You Have Achieved
- **Rigorous Thinking:** Writing deterministic, memory-safe, crash-resilient code.
- **Data Architecture:** Structuring complex real-world entities into clean models.
- **Algorithmic Mastery:** Navigating 2D spaces, optimizing resources, and filtering sensor noise.
- **Professional Presentation:** Formatted reporting, robust error recovery, and modular design.

Robot mascot **IRIS [ o o ]** and the entire squadron salute you. Submit your final capstone project for grading, review your flight logs, and carry your C++ engineering mastery into the next frontier!
